title: Stub-proxy contract suite for retry/backpressure and streaming ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a cross-language contract test suite that runs against a lightweight stub-proxy to validate retry semantics, streaming ergonomics, and backpressure handling across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The goal is deterministic, CI-friendly tests that catch regressions in: (a) client retry policies and idempotency keys, (b) partial/early stream termination and resumption behavior, (c) artificial backpressure and batching interaction with KV cache usage, and (d) error mapping consistency between SDKs and the Redwood API. This ticket covers harness design, example contracts for canonical flows, tooling to drive the stub from each SDK, and CI integration.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible stub-proxy binary or Docker image that can simulate: 1) transient HTTP 5xx/429 with configurable retry-after, 2) chunked stream delays and mid-stream aborts, 3) connection resets and slow-read backpressure

A set of contract tests implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go that assert SDK behavior against the stub (retry counts, idempotency token usage, backoff timing tolerance, event ordering on streams)
Tests run deterministically in CI with recorded deterministic fixtures and time controls; failures produce actionable diffs and links to failing SDK logs
A short how-to doc and example commands so engineers can run the suite locally and add new contracts (README under tests/contract-suite)
Integration in CI pipeline gated on SDK PRs; at least one blocking test added to the SDK release pipeline
test_plan: Design matrix: language x scenario matrix (happy path streaming, mid-stream abort, exponential backoff, 429 throttling, large-token batch flushing)
Create canonical input prompts and simulated server behaviors (delay profiles, error injection timelines)
Implement language drivers: python/driver.py, ts/driver.ts, go/driver.go that orchestrate the stub and assert expectations
Add deterministic fixtures capture mode: capture responses from the stub-proxy and compare against golden fixtures in CI; provide --regen flag for maintainers
Run full matrix on PRs that modify retry/streaming code; lightweight smoke tests on every commit
mock_server_details: Prototype: small Go stub-proxy (single binary) with table-driven scenarios and a JSON control socket to trigger timelines
Modes: record (produce fixtures), replay (serve recorded streams identically), and fuzz (randomized delays/errors)
Supports HTTP/1.1 chunked responses and HTTP/2 streams to mirror hosted API behavior
Configuration: per-endpoint scenario files under tests/stub-configs/*.json; CI loads a deterministic seed for replay mode
implementation_notes: Prefer a Go binary due to fast startup in CI and easy cross-compilation; provide a Docker image for reproducibility
Expose a lightweight control API (localhost) so language drivers can coordinate start/stop and inject mid-stream events
Keep the protocol between SDK drivers and stub intentionally simple (newline-delimited JSON commands) to avoid adding new SDK network surfaces
Time control: inject virtual time where possible (test harness sleeps are mocked) or run with scaled delays to keep CI runtime reasonable
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-02-25: go-stub chosen over WireMock due to streaming control and deterministic replay requirements
We will not try to simulate full auth flows in the stub; drivers will inject a bearer token that the stub validates against a fixed test value
Idempotency token format: UUIDv4 string required for retry-sensitive contract tests
